overall: The Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by convening in executive session for an improper purpose and by failing to vote by roll call; no violation on notice or complainant attendance; minutes ordered amended and released.

allegations.summary: Commission allegedly convened in executive session on June 11, 2024 for an improper purpose, discussing whether to seek Town Counsel advice on a prior complaint.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by convening in executive session for an improper purpose.

allegations.summary: Commission allegedly convened in executive session on June 11, 2024 by voice vote ('All in favor') rather than a roll call vote.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to vote by roll call to convene in executive session on June 11, 2024.

allegations.summary: Commission allegedly discussed in executive session a matter not listed on the June 11, 2024 notice (the approved RDA at 6 Molasses Hill Road).
Complainant alleges the Commission did not allow them to attend the June 11, 2024 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: whether or not an individual, such as the complainant, is permitted to participate in an executive session is a matter at the discretion of the Commission and its decision to restrict an individual’s attendance at an executive session meeting would not be a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Not raised as a separate allegation; the AG reviewed the June 11, 2024 executive session draft minutes and found them insufficient on their face.
allegations.key_passage: With respect to the minutes of the executive session, we find them to be insufficient.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
Within 30 days, amend the June 11, 2024 executive session minutes to accurately summarize the discussion, approve and release them to the public, and certify compliance to the AG.
remedy_passage: we order the Commission, within 30 days of the date of this letter, to amend the minutes of its June 11, 2024, executive session to accurately summarize its discussion, to approve and release such minutes to the public, and to certify to this office that it has done so.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
